items.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: the violin with Feldman, because the band has really been going in a more outer direction with Mark in it

ctx.x: But you’re bound to satisfy yourself one way or the other.

Yeah. I try to make myself feel good about what I’m playing. To the band tonight, it would be interesting to see which directions we take. We’ll probably play some a little more traditional things than we would normally do with the violin with Feldman, because the band has really been going in a more outer direction with Mark in it, playing a lot of very abstract kind of pieces. With the trio we might come a little more inside. It’ll be interesting to see what we do.

I’ve always been fascinated by the challenge of hearing I guess what you would call alternate chord changes. If your organist decides to start some new substitutions that you haven’t heard before, how do you nail those? Or do you?
